I want to become an artist. I'm mostly interested in concept art and graphic design, but I'm young and am open to other opportunities. I love art. It's the one thing that makes feel really happy. Whether it's visualising my or others' creative ideas, I'm happy. Even if I'm nowhere near the level I want to be, drawing and developing my skills makes me happy. It's the type of work I'm happy to do.

I'm currently in high school. I know doing well in high school is important. It's why I didn't go directly to an art school, because it's helpful to have as many options open as possible. But school exhausts me. I don't just feel tired, I feel so fatigued, that all I want to do is just pass out. So I gather enough energy to do my homework, and then I go to bed and pass out. I also take ballet lessons three times a week, which often doesn't leave me with enough time to complete all my homework.

The education system in my country covers a lot of breadth but not enough depth. We have 12 obligatory subjects. It's really hard to do well in each one when I only really care about a few.

Basically, because I'm so fixated on school, and also receive pressure from my mother to do well ( I know she wants me to get good grades, so that I can do well later on in life, but she shows it by nagging me to work even harder, which puts me under even more pressure), I don't have enough time to practice drawing and painting. And it makes me want to cry my heart out, because without being able to creatively express myself, I end up feeling empty, depressed and generally just sad. When there's a day where I didn't have enough time to do any drawing at all, I feel so awful. It's painful.

Maybe I sound like a desperate teenager (which I probably am), but it feels good to write this down.
Studying for school doesn't leave me with enough time to pursue my passion, and it's making me depressed.
